current.title: Ulysses
current.author: James Joyce
current.review: Started this ahead of a trip to Ireland. I've read the Odyssey and the Bible, speak a little French and Latin, and it still took me three tries to get through the first four chapters—-plus, I needed the Gilbert Schema and one of my friends to do it. This is literally my own personal Odyssey.

shelf.title: Ted Lasso S1-4
shelf.author: cr. Jason Sudeikis, Bill Lawrence, Brendan Hunt, and Joe Kelly
shelf.review: Comfort rewatch. This show got me through most of high school, and the belief that people can always work to be the best version of themselves still carries me through life.

shelf.title: Deli Boys
shelf.author: cr. Abdullah Saeed
shelf.review: Watching this with my little sister. We're big fans of the violence (and Poorna Jagannathan in anything).

shelf.title: Banshees of Inisherin
shelf.author: dir. Martin McDonagh
shelf.review: Airplane movie heading into Dublin! The cinematography is so evocative, and the cliffs of Ireland are so beautiful. I think about Pádraig, Siobhan, and Colm often.

shelf.title: Katabasis
shelf.author: R.F. Kuang
shelf.review: The antagonist and characters were kind of soapy and predictable, but what a fun read! I especially loved the paradox-based magic system.

shelf.title: Butter
shelf.author: Asako Yuzuki
shelf.review: I really loved this one. Like the high-end butter and rice she describes, her prose excites the tongue, clings to the throat and warms the body. Yuzuki's food descriptions are so vivid, and all her characters have so much depth. This is actually what made me leave IQ84 alone.

shelf.title: IQ84
shelf.author: Haruki Murakami
shelf.review: I honestly couldn't finish this because of how glaring and distracting Murakami's misogyny is in any female character's description. Tough read.
